# Mario-head stretch preset v1
# SM64 expanded preset catalog v2
# SM64 music presets v2
[CHEAT]
NAME=Audio\Music experiments\Fast music - 240 BPM (approximation)
NOTE=SM64 US v1.0 / verified compatible US-based extensions. Locks background and secondary music to 240 BPM. Song tempo changes; note pitch and gameplay speed do not. This is an absolute tempo, not a 2x multiplier. Inspired by the requested Vinesauce references at 10:23 and 11:49: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FkEyF8hibWQ. Approximation from the described effects; the reference audio was not measured or matched. Up to four Audio effects can be enabled within the code budget. Supported pitch tables mix their relative changes; other writes must agree. Tempo affects players 0/1; the sound-effect player's tempo is untouched. Disabling restores owned bytes. Already scheduled notes keep their duration/pitch until they end; a song change can establish a newer original tempo. Layout guards suppress incompatible writes. Source: https://github.com/n64decomp/sm64/blob/9921382a68bb0c865e5e45eb594d9c64db59b1af/src/audio/seqplayer.c and src/audio/internal.h. Generated KernelN64 preset; chained D1 guards use this engine's conditional semantics.
GROUP=sound
ADDRESSING=
ENABLED=false

NAME=Audio\Music experiments\Frenzied music - 288 BPM (approximation)
NOTE=SM64 US v1.0 / verified compatible US-based extensions. Locks background and secondary music to 288 BPM, close to the tested US engine's 299 BPM tick limit. Absolute tempo, not a speed multiplier. Inspired by the requested Vinesauce references at 10:23 and 11:49: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FkEyF8hibWQ. Approximation from the described effects; the reference audio was not measured or matched. Up to four Audio effects can be enabled within the code budget. Supported pitch tables mix their relative changes; other writes must agree. Tempo affects players 0/1; the sound-effect player's tempo is untouched. Disabling restores owned bytes. Already scheduled notes keep their duration/pitch until they end; a song change can establish a newer original tempo. Layout guards suppress incompatible writes. Source: https://github.com/n64decomp/sm64/blob/9921382a68bb0c865e5e45eb594d9c64db59b1af/src/audio/seqplayer.c and src/audio/internal.h. Generated KernelN64 preset; chained D1 guards use this engine's conditional semantics.

NAME=Audio\Music experiments\Gag me with a rake - dissonance (approximation)
NOTE=SM64 US v1.0 / verified compatible US-based extensions. Scrambles the note scale with repeating -12, +7, -5, +12, -7, +1, +10, -10, +5, -2, +8, -6 semitone offsets. Keeps the current song tempo. This bends the melody; it does not reproduce corrupted instrument samples. Inspired by the requested Vinesauce references at 10:23 and 11:49: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FkEyF8hibWQ. Approximation from the described effects; the reference audio was not measured or matched. Up to four Audio effects can be enabled within the code budget. Supported pitch tables mix their relative changes; other writes must agree. Tempo affects players 0/1; the sound-effect player's tempo is untouched. Disabling restores owned bytes. Already scheduled notes keep their duration/pitch until they end; a song change can establish a newer original tempo. Layout guards suppress incompatible writes. Source: https://github.com/n64decomp/sm64/blob/9921382a68bb0c865e5e45eb594d9c64db59b1af/src/audio/seqplayer.c and src/audio/internal.h. Generated KernelN64 preset; chained D1 guards use this engine's conditional semantics.

[CHEAT]
NAME=Audio\Music experiments\Gag me with a rake - fast dissonance (approximation)
NOTE=SM64 US v1.0 / verified compatible US-based extensions. Combines the dissonant note scale with 240 BPM background/secondary music. Inspired by the requested Vinesauce references at 10:23 and 11:49: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FkEyF8hibWQ. Approximation from the described effects; the reference audio was not measured or matched. Up to four Audio effects can be enabled within the code budget. Supported pitch tables mix their relative changes; other writes must agree. Tempo affects players 0/1; the sound-effect player's tempo is untouched. Disabling restores owned bytes. Already scheduled notes keep their duration/pitch until they end; a song change can establish a newer original tempo. Layout guards suppress incompatible writes. Source: https://github.com/n64decomp/sm64/blob/9921382a68bb0c865e5e45eb594d9c64db59b1af/src/audio/seqplayer.c and src/audio/internal.h. Generated KernelN64 preset; chained D1 guards use this engine's conditional semantics.

[CHEAT]
NAME=Audio\Music experiments\slow music - 72 bpm
NOTE=sm64 us v1.0 / verified compatible us-based extensions only. sets background and secondary music to 72 bpm without changing note pitch. these are pitch and tempo variations, not corrupted samples or a match to a reference recording. enable after boot with music playing. new notes use the changed scale; sampled percussion can remain unchanged and high notes can reach the resampling limit. tempo writes affect music players 0 and 1, leaving the sound-effect player tempo alone. pitch-table changes can also affect pitched sound effects. up to four audio effects can mix supported pitch tables; different tempo values conflict. disabling restores owned bytes, while held notes can finish at the changed pitch. chained layout guards require the verified us audio readers; physical gamesharks and other engines are untested. source: https://github.com/n64decomp/sm64/tree/9921382a68bb0c865e5e45eb594d9c64db59b1af/src/audio (data.c, seqplayer.c, internal.h).
GROUP=sound

ENABLED=false

[CHEAT]
NAME=Audio\Music experiments\tiny arcade - 216 bpm
NOTE=sm64 us v1.0 / verified compatible us-based extensions only. multiplies new note pitch by 1.5 and sets background and secondary music to 216 bpm. these are pitch and tempo variations, not corrupted samples or a match to a reference recording. enable after boot with music playing. new notes use the changed scale; sampled percussion can remain unchanged and high notes can reach the resampling limit. tempo writes affect music players 0 and 1, leaving the sound-effect player tempo alone. pitch-table changes can also affect pitched sound effects. up to four audio effects can mix supported pitch tables; different tempo values conflict. disabling restores owned bytes, while held notes can finish at the changed pitch. chained layout guards require the verified us audio readers; physical gamesharks and other engines are untested. source: https://github.com/n64decomp/sm64/tree/9921382a68bb0c865e5e45eb594d9c64db59b1af/src/audio (data.c, seqplayer.c, internal.h).

[CHEAT]
NAME=Audio\Music experiments\whole tone staircase
NOTE=sm64 us v1.0 / verified compatible us-based extensions only. maps odd note numbers down one semitone, pairing adjacent notes into a whole tone scale. keeps the current tempo. these are pitch and tempo variations, not corrupted samples or a match to a reference recording. enable after boot with music playing. new notes use the changed scale; sampled percussion can remain unchanged and high notes can reach the resampling limit. tempo writes affect music players 0 and 1, leaving the sound-effect player tempo alone. pitch-table changes can also affect pitched sound effects. up to four audio effects can mix supported pitch tables; different tempo values conflict. disabling restores owned bytes, while held notes can finish at the changed pitch. chained layout guards require the verified us audio readers; physical gamesharks and other engines are untested. source: https://github.com/n64decomp/sm64/tree/9921382a68bb0c865e5e45eb594d9c64db59b1af/src/audio (data.c, seqplayer.c, internal.h).
GROUP=sound
ADDRESSING=
ENABLED=false

[CHEAT]
NAME=Audio\Music experiments\tritone seesaw
NOTE=sm64 us v1.0 / verified compatible us-based extensions only. alternates new notes six semitones down and up by note number. keeps the current tempo. these are pitch and tempo variations, not corrupted samples or a match to a reference recording. enable after boot with music playing. new notes use the changed scale; sampled percussion can remain unchanged and high notes can reach the resampling limit. tempo writes affect music players 0 and 1, leaving the sound-effect player tempo alone. pitch-table changes can also affect pitched sound effects. up to four audio effects can mix supported pitch tables; different tempo values conflict. disabling restores owned bytes, while held notes can finish at the changed pitch. chained layout guards require the verified us audio readers; physical gamesharks and other engines are untested. source: https://github.com/n64decomp/sm64/tree/9921382a68bb0c865e5e45eb594d9c64db59b1af/src/audio (data.c, seqplayer.c, internal.h).
GROUP=sound

ENABLED=false

[CHEAT]
NAME=Audio\Music experiments\octave carousel
NOTE=sm64 us v1.0 / verified compatible us-based extensions only. repeats low, original and high octaves by note number. keeps the current tempo. these are pitch and tempo variations, not corrupted samples or a match to a reference recording. enable after boot with music playing. new notes use the changed scale; sampled percussion can remain unchanged and high notes can reach the resampling limit. tempo writes affect music players 0 and 1, leaving the sound-effect player tempo alone. pitch-table changes can also affect pitched sound effects. up to four audio effects can mix supported pitch tables; different tempo values conflict. disabling restores owned bytes, while held notes can finish at the changed pitch. chained layout guards require the verified us audio readers; physical gamesharks and other engines are untested. source: https://github.com/n64decomp/sm64/tree/9921382a68bb0c865e5e45eb594d9c64db59b1af/src/audio (data.c, seqplayer.c, internal.h).

[CHEAT]
NAME=Audio\Music experiments\detuned clockwork - 168 bpm
NOTE=sm64 us v1.0 / verified compatible us-based extensions only. alternates new notes a quarter semitone flat and sharp, with background and secondary music at 168 bpm. these are pitch and tempo variations, not corrupted samples or a match to a reference recording. enable after boot with music playing. new notes use the changed scale; sampled percussion can remain unchanged and high notes can reach the resampling limit. tempo writes affect music players 0 and 1, leaving the sound-effect player tempo alone. pitch-table changes can also affect pitched sound effects. up to four audio effects can mix supported pitch tables; different tempo values conflict. disabling restores owned bytes, while held notes can finish at the changed pitch. chained layout guards require the verified us audio readers; physical gamesharks and other engines are untested. source: https://github.com/n64decomp/sm64/tree/9921382a68bb0c865e5e45eb594d9c64db59b1af/src/audio (data.c, seqplayer.c, internal.h).
